free_tier.stated: No free tier. The IPv6-only plan is EUR 11.99 a year: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD, 1 TB traffic, one IPv6 address up to a /52, KVM, IPv6 only with no IPv4.

retention.stated: annual billing; the order form offers 1 month, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year on the Amsterdam rung and 1 year only on Frankfurt and Toronto. No deletion grace period is printed.

egress.terms: 1 TB on the IPv6-only plan; the plan card states 'Traffic 1 TB' and the uplink as 1 Gbit/s fair-share

interface_detail: KVM with full root access, Proxmox web panel with VNC console, standard Linux distributions or a custom ISO. IPv6 is one address up to a /52; there is no IPv4 on the plan.
tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; a free BGP session with AS11967 and an optional additional IPv6 subnet are offered as add-ons
chaining: a routing-lab-grade IPv6 box for EUR 1 a month: free BGP transit, a /52 available, and a real routed address rather than a forwarded port

limits.value: 1 TB a month on the IPv6-only plan
1 Gbit/s fair-share uplink; no byte threshold for shaping is published

binding_note: 1 TB a month is the first ceiling a VPN node reaches, and the annual-only term on Frankfurt means the whole year is paid before that is tested.

identity_cost.detail: a Blesta client account; the checkout form was not read. No card hold is stated on any page read. The order page is a plain POST form and the client area is my.hop179.net.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the vendor states 'All VPSes are provisioned manually within a few hours. We do not use any automated provisioning system.'
confidence_note: price, shape, the IPv6-only statement, the /52, stock and the term options are read from the vendor's own order page today. The cart is a POST form rather than a GET cart URL, so the deepest clickable link is the package page plus the pricing_id the form submits.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'Frankfurt VPS ... CPU1 Core ... Disk10 GB SSD ... Memory1 GB ... Traffic1 TB ... 11.99€ Per Year ... * excl. VAT' with an 'Order Now' link to https://my.hop179.net/order/main/packages/v6-vps

quoted order page: 'Frankfurt VPS (V6 Only) vCPU: 1 core (Intel Xeon E) RAM: 1 GB Disk: 10 GB Bandwidth: 1 Gbit/s (fair-share) IPv4: none IPv6: 1 (up to /52)' and '1 Year @ €11.99 EUR' with an 'Add to Cart' button; the form posts to /order/main/packages/v6-vps/?group_id=11 with pricing_id=98

quoted stock state: the Amsterdam card shows 'Out of Stock' with a disabled button, Frankfurt shows 'Add to Cart', Toronto shows 'Out of Stock'. Amsterdam prices 1 Month @ €1.00, 3 Months @ €3.00, 6 Months @ €6.00, 1 Year @ €11.99
quoted IPv4 add-on ladder: 'IPv4 /32 1 IPs Total 2 EUR/month (20 EUR/year) ... Available: yes' - so an IPv4 address is EUR 2 a month extra, which more than doubles this plan
page title reads 'IPv6 Only Virtual Servers | Hop179 OÜ', naming the legal entity as an Estonian OÜ

notes: The best per-dollar shape among the rows that are actually buyable today: 1 GB and 10 GB for EUR 11.99 a year is EUR 0.999 a month, and the plan carries a /52 rather than a single /128, which is enough for a routed subnet behind the guest. The catch is the IPv4 add-on: at EUR 2 a month it is 24 EUR a year on top of an 11.99 EUR plan, so converting this row to dual-stack triples it. Frankfurt is the only IPv6 rung in stock on 2026-10-24; Amsterdam and Toronto both read Out of Stock. Not established: the checkout fields, payment rails, any card hold, and whether the 'up to /52' is a routed prefix or a pool the panel hands out one address from.
